acceptanceCriteria.criterion: Pre-production is independently isolated from development and production data, credentials, and network policy.
Provider credentials are encrypted at rest and never exposed to the frontend.
Credential rotation is demonstrated without data loss or unauthorized access.
Credential and OAuth revocation is demonstrated and audited.
Tenant isolation passes read and write denial tests.
Only owner-approved shops and SKU ranges can enter a gray stage.
Real Provider authentication succeeds only in the approved environment and scope.
The real read golden path returns validated, normalized, tenant-scoped data.
Rate limits, timeouts, 429, 5xx, token expiry, and refresh failure have bounded safe handling.
Provider errors map to safe internal errors without credential or raw-response leakage.
Unauthorized real inventory write is impossible at L0-L2.
PostgreSQL backup completes with integrity evidence against the owner-approved RPO.
A restore drill meets the owner-approved RTO and validates application consistency.
Deployment and migration rollback are demonstrated from a controlled failure.
Provider kill switch stops all real-provider calls within the approved response time.
Tenant and shop kill switches isolate only the selected scope.
Read and write kill switches are independently testable and fail closed.
Threat review, secret scan, SAST, dependency scan, container scan, permission review, and adversarial testing pass.
A dedicated-host fixed B1-C1-C2-B2 validation matrix completes and is valid for formal planning.
Formal P50, P95, P99, throughput, concurrency, error-rate, CPU, memory, DB-connection, and provider-limit evidence meets approved thresholds.
At least 30 minutes of soak plus demo x2, stability, race, and cleanup pass on the dedicated host.
Provider, OAuth, inventory sync, backlog, database, host, and security-denial telemetry is queryable and correlated.
Actionable alerts fire and recover during controlled provider, OAuth, database, and security failures.
Read-only G1 and G2 meet entry, exit, observation, metric, rollback, kill-switch, and approver requirements.
The named Gray Go/No-Go approver records an explicit decision from complete evidence.
Release integrity binds source, artifacts, configuration, migrations, and acceptance evidence.
The named final owner explicitly approves Production Ready after all blocking criteria pass.
If D04/D05 are approved, controlled writes require per-operation confirmation, idempotency, audit, bounded retry, and write-incident rollback evidence.
